sub: Named after al-Ghāshiyah, “the Overwhelming”, in ayah 1
theme: The Overwhelming Day splits people into two groups. The signs around them prove Allah can do it, and the Prophet ﷺ’s task is only to remind.
story: An early Makkan surah, from the time the Prophet ﷺ had begun preaching openly. People heard his message about tawḥīd and the Hereafter and brushed it off without thinking.

It shakes them with a question about the Overwhelming Day and shows the two groups: exhausted faces in the Fire, joyful faces in a high garden. Then it points to things they see every day: camels, sky, mountains, earth.
The Prophet ﷺ recited it with Al-Aʿlā in the Eid and Friday prayers. It closes by reminding him that he is only a reminder: the return and the reckoning belong to Allah.

sections.title: The Overwhelming Day: humbled faces burn, drink boiling water and eat thorns
sections.meaning: Has news of the Overwhelming Day reached you? Some faces that Day will be humbled, toiling and exhausted. They burn in a scorching Fire, drink from a boiling spring, and eat only a bitter thorn that neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger.
points: Has news of al-Ghāshiyah reached you?
A scorching Fire and a boiling spring
Only ḍarīʿ: no nourishment, no relief from hunger
sections.matters: It opens with a question to wake heedless people up, then shows the losing side first. Every need, heat, thirst and hunger, is answered with more pain.
sections.story: When ayah 6 described ḍarīʿ as the food of Hell, the idolaters of Makkah mocked: “Our camels grow fat on ḍarīʿ.” Ayah 7 answered them: this food neither fattens nor ends hunger.
explained: Al-Ghāshiyah is the Day of Resurrection, named because its terrors overwhelm everyone. Some faces that Day are khāshiʿah, low and disgraced. ʿĀmilah nāṣibah: labouring and worn out, either toiling in the Fire, or people who worked hard at worship in this world on a wrong path, gaining nothing.

They enter a Fire ḥāmiyah, burning at full heat, and drink from a spring āniyah, boiling to its limit. Their only food is ḍarīʿ, a dry, poisonous thorn no animal will touch. Food is meant to end hunger or build the body; this does neither.
teaches: Hard work only counts when it rests on true faith.
Don’t mock warnings about the Hereafter.
Humble your face before Allah now, or it will be humbled then.
sections.hook: The surah opens with a question, hal atāka (1). “Faces that Day”, wujūhun yawmaʾidhin, opens this section (2) and the next (8).

sections.title: Radiant faces, pleased with their effort, in a high garden with couches
sections.meaning: Other faces that Day are radiant, pleased with the effort they made, in a lofty garden. No idle talk is heard there. It has a flowing spring, raised couches, cups set ready, cushions in rows, and carpets spread everywhere.
points: Faces glowing, pleased with their effort
A high garden with no empty talk
Cups set out, cushions lined up, carpets spread
sections.matters: It is the mirror image of section 1: joy for exhaustion, a flowing spring for a boiling one, comfort for thorns. And it ties the reward to saʿy, the effort made in this life.
sections.story: No specific incident. It completes the picture of the Overwhelming Day by describing the people of Paradise.
explained: Some faces that Day are nāʿimah, glowing with blessing. Li-saʿyihā rāḍiyah: pleased with the good they sent ahead, now that they see it rewarded. They are in a garden high in place and rank, where no lāghiyah is heard: no foolish, false or hurtful word.

A spring flows there, meaning many springs. Couches are raised high. Cups are set out, ready. Namāriq, cushions, are lined up side by side, and zarābiyy, fine carpets, are spread everywhere. Everything is already in place for them.
teaches: Effort for Allah now becomes joy later.
Guard your tongue: Paradise is free of idle and hurtful talk.
Keep shared things in their place; the cups of Paradise are set ready.
sections.hook: Fīhā (“in it”) repeats: 11, 12, 13. Then four furnishings (13–16), each followed by one describing word: marfūʿah, mawḍūʿah, maṣfūfah, mabthūthah.

sections.title: Look at the camel, sky and mountains; you only remind, Allah judges
sections.meaning: Do they not look at how the camel was created, how the sky was raised, the mountains set up and the earth spread out? So remind: you are only a reminder, not a controller. Whoever turns away and disbelieves gets the greatest punishment. To Us is their return, and on Us their account.
points: Look at the camel, how it was created
The sky raised, mountains set firm, earth spread out
So remind: you are not their controller
Whoever turns away faces the greatest punishment
Their return is to Us, their reckoning on Us
sections.matters: After the Day comes the proof. A desert traveller sees these four signs on every journey; if Allah made them, He can raise the dead. And the Prophet ﷺ is freed from forcing faith: reminding is his job, reckoning is Allah’s.
sections.story: Reportedly, when the raised couches of Paradise were mentioned, the disbelievers asked how they could climb them. Ayah 17 pointed to the camel, which kneels to be loaded and then rises.
explained: Look at what is right in front of you: the camel you ride, huge and strong yet led by a child, able to go days without water; the sky raised above you with no pillars; the mountains planted firm so the earth stays steady; the earth spread out to live and travel on. Who made all this?

So remind, fa-dhakkir. You are only a mudhakkir, a reminder, not a muṣayṭir who forces faith into hearts. Whoever turns away and disbelieves gets al-ʿadhāb al-akbar, the punishment of the Hereafter. Their return is to Allah, and their reckoning is His.
teaches: Reflect on ordinary creation; it points to the Creator.
Your job is to remind, not to force anyone’s heart.
Leave results and reckoning to Allah.
Turning away from the truth has the heaviest cost.
sections.hook: Four “how” (kayfa) questions in a row (17–20): camel, sky, mountains, earth. The surah ends with two matching lines, inna ilaynā (25) and inna ʿalaynā (26): return, then account.

groups.text: Has news of the Overwhelming Day reached you? Some faces that Day will be humbled, toiling and worn out.
They burn in a scorching Fire and drink from a boiling spring.
Their only food is a poisonous thorn that neither fattens nor ends hunger.
Other faces are joyful, pleased with their effort, in a lofty garden.
No idle talk is heard there; it has a flowing spring and raised couches.
Cups set ready, cushions in rows, carpets spread everywhere.
Do they not look at the camel, how it was created?
And the sky raised, the mountains set up, and the earth spread out?
So remind: you are only a reminder, not a controller over them.
Whoever turns away and disbelieves, Allah will punish with the greatest punishment.
Their return is to Us, and their reckoning is on Us.

1.explain: Hal atāka: has it reached you? Al-Ghāshiyah, the Overwhelming, is the Day of Resurrection, covering all creation with its terrors.

2.explain: Wujūh: faces, meaning the people themselves. Khāshiʿah: humbled and disgraced. Those who never lowered themselves before Allah are lowered now.

3.explain: ʿĀmilah nāṣibah: toiling and exhausted. Either labouring in the Fire, or people who strained in worship on a wrong path in this world, and it counted for nothing.

4.explain: Taṣlā: they enter and burn in a Fire ḥāmiyah, intensely hot and surrounding them. Unlike fire in this world, its heat never fades.

5.explain: Their drink comes from ʿayn āniyah, a spring boiling at its highest heat.

6.explain: Their only food is ḍarīʿ: a thorny plant, called shibriq when green, poisonous and foul once dry, which no animal will graze.

7.explain: It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger. Food exists to do one of those two things; this does neither.
7.why: When ayah 6 was revealed, the idolaters said, “Our camels grow fat on ḍarīʿ.” This ayah answered them. They were wrong: camels only graze it while it is green.

8.explain: Other faces are nāʿimah: soft and radiant with blessing, their joy plain to see.

9.explain: Li-saʿyihā rāḍiyah: pleased with the effort they made in the world, now that they find its reward stored up and multiplied.

10.explain: In a jannah ʿāliyah: a garden high in place and in rank.

11.explain: Lā tasmaʿu fīhā lāghiyah: no idle, false or hurtful word is heard there. Their speech is good and full of remembering Allah.

12.explain: ʿAyn jāriyah: a flowing spring. The word stands for many springs, running wherever they wish.

13.explain: Surur marfūʿah: couches raised high, lofty in themselves and in the soft furnishings on them.

14.explain: Akwāb mawḍūʿah: cups set out ready and close at hand, filled with delicious drinks.

15.explain: Namāriq maṣfūfah: cushions lined up side by side for leaning on, arranged without their lifting a finger.

16.explain: Zarābiyy mabthūthah: fine carpets spread out, filling their sitting places on every side.

17.explain: Do they not reflect on the camel? Strong, carrying heavy loads, yet led by a child; giving milk, meat and hair. It was the Arabs’ most familiar animal.
17.why: Reportedly, when the raised couches of Paradise were described, they asked, “How do we climb them?” This came: the camel kneels to be loaded, then rises.

18.explain: And the sky: how it was raised so high above the earth, without pillars.

19.explain: And the mountains: how they were set firmly in place, keeping the earth stable, with benefits and minerals stored inside them.

20.explain: And the earth: how it was spread wide and made easy to live on, farm, build on and travel across.

21.explain: Fa-dhakkir: so remind them of Allah’s blessings and signs. Innamā anta mudhakkir: that is your whole task.

22.explain: Lasta ʿalayhim bi-muṣayṭir: you are not a controller over them. You cannot put faith in their hearts or force it. This came before fighting was ordered.

23.explain: Illā man tawallā wa kafar: but whoever turns away from obedience and disbelieves after being reminded…

24.explain: …Allah will punish him with al-ʿadhāb al-akbar, the greatest punishment: the Fire of the Hereafter. Hardship in this world is the lesser one.

25.explain: Inna ilaynā iyābahum: to Us is their return, gathered after death.

26.explain: Then on Us is their ḥisāb: their account and recompense, good for good and evil for evil. Allah never leaves it undone.
